issues.description: Unbounded in-memory log buffer with no cap or eviction policy
issues.detail: _BufferingHandler stores every LogRecord in a Python list until either init_recording flushes it or _stop_log_buffering drops it. If a session hangs between _on_setup and any cleanup path (e.g. stuck in connect retries or a slow loop), this grows without bound. State the invariant: 'buffer holds at most N records or M bytes.' Add a ring-buffer cap.

issues.description: Replay loop is O(H*B) and silently no-ops if OTLP handler missing
issues.detail: _flush_early_log_buffer scans root handlers for a LoggingHandler and breaks on the first match; if init_recording installed it on a non-root logger or ordering changes, replay silently drops every buffered record. State the postcondition explicitly and assert at least one handler was found, or log a warning. Also document why only the first match is correct.

issues.description: Shutdown handler removal mutates list during iteration semantics is fragile
issues.detail: _shutdown_telemetry iterates root.handlers[:] and removes LoggingHandler instances, but the rationale ('avoid deadlock from re-entrant emit during force_flush') deserves a literate comment naming exactly which call path re-enters. Without that invariant stated, a future reader restoring the handler post-flush will reintroduce the deadlock. The slice copy is correct; the reasoning is what needs preserving.

issues.description: Concurrent set_result race on _shutdown_fut suppressed without invariant
issues.detail: _on_entry_done uses contextlib.suppress(InvalidStateError) to handle the case where _shutdown_fut already resolved. The suppression is correct but the invariant ('shutdown_fut is set at most once; first writer wins; crash reason may be lost if connect path won the race') should be stated in a comment so the next reader does not 'fix' it.

issues.description: Removing -n auto and skipping google STT test is unexplained regression in test rigor
issues.detail: The makefile change drops parallel pytest execution and excludes test_plugin_google_stt.py with no comment or commit rationale visible in the diff. This is the kind of silent change that haunts future maintainers: a reader cannot tell if -n auto was flaky, if the google test is broken, or if this is temporary. State why, or revert.

issues.description: init_recording reentry path stops buffering but leaves no audit trail of dropped records
issues.detail: When init_recording is called but recording was already initialized or not cloud, _stop_log_buffering drops the entire buffer without replay or count. For a feature whose purpose is troubleshooting crashes, silently discarding N buffered records deserves at least a debug log of len(buffer) so operators can detect the silent-drop case.

review.summary: The crash-log upload path is structurally sound and the deadlock-avoidance fix in _shutdown_telemetry is the right shape, but the diff is UNDER-AUDITED in the Knuth sense: invariants are unstated and the buffering structure has no cap. The _BufferingHandler is an unbounded list — fine for a fast-failing crash, dangerous for a slow hang. Replay logic depends on handler ordering and silently no-ops if assumptions break; both deserve literate comments and at least one assertion. The makefile changes (dropping -n auto, excluding google STT test) are unexplained and reduce test rigor without a stated reason. Verdict: NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT and a bounded buffer before merge.
